issues.description: Method PersonResource.createPerson has an inconsistent return type and error-handling contract compared to the notes resource and the problem statement. The problem statement (POST /persons) expects the saved Person to be returned in the HTTP response body (see problem_statement.md lines 109-113). In the solution, NoteResource.createNote uses ResponseEntity<Note> and returns ResponseEntity.badRequest().build() for invalid input (solution/src/server/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/rest/NoteResource.java, signature at lines 30-31). By contrast, the solution's PersonResource.createPerson is declared to return a raw Person and returns null for invalid input instead of a ResponseEntity (solution/src/server/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/rest/PersonResource.java, @PostMapping method signature at lines 29-31). This difference in return type (Person vs ResponseEntity<Person>) and the use of null instead of an HTTP error response is likely to confuse students about the expected endpoint contract and recommended implementation style.
issues.suggestedFix: Make PersonResource#createPerson consistent with NoteResource and the problem statement: change the method signature to return ResponseEntity<Person> and return ResponseEntity.badRequest().build() for invalid input. Example: public ResponseEntity<Person> createPerson(@RequestBody Person person) { if (person.getId() != null) { return ResponseEntity.badRequest().build(); } return ResponseEntity.ok(personService.savePerson(person)); } This preserves the API contract and consistent error handling across resources.
